extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, psychophysicists, and ERP researchers studying face perception and adaptation
extracted.subtask_short: ERP adaptation study for face processing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and analysing an event-related potential (ERP) adaptation experiment that tests how manipulations of first- and second-order facial configurations affect behavioral aftereffects and early face-sensitive ERP components (especially the N170).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish first-order and second-order relations (CONF1st, CONF2nd)
rubrics_metrics.description: First-order relational information (CONF1st) is the basic feature configuration that distinguishes faces from non-face objects; second-order relational information (CONF2nd) refers to metric variations (spatial distances) among facial features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly define and manipulate CONF1st vs CONF2nd when testing configural processing hypotheses; interpret results with respect to whether effects reflect category-level (first-order) or fine-grained (second-order) configural information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a long adaptation duration to induce robust aftereffects
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply long-term adaptation to adapter faces (here: 5000 ms) before presenting test faces to elicit robust behavioral and ERP adaptation effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper used 5000 ms adaptors followed by a 550 ms gap and a 200 ms test stimulus; this timing has been shown to produce strong N170 reductions in prior work (e.g., Kovacs et al., 2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a non-face control adapter (Fourier phase-randomized) to assess category-level adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a Fourier phase-randomized version of a face (preserving amplitude spectrum but removing shape information) as a control (CTRL) adapter to determine category-level N170 adaptation effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare NORM and STR adapters to CTRL to identify face-specific adaptation versus non-face baselines; reason for inclusion is to assess categorical N170 adaptation (Kovacs et al., 2006, 2007; Kloth et al., 2010).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulate adapter configuration and gender systematically (NORM, STR; male, female)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use adapters differing by configuration (normal proportions vs vertically stretched) and by gender (male, female) to test their separate and interactive effects on aftereffects and ERP adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all combinations (NORM_F, NORM_M, STR_F, STR_M) and analyze adapter configuration × adapter gender interactions when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present adapters in separate pseudo-randomized blocks with short breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the five adapter conditions in separate blocks presented in a pseudo-randomized order, with short breaks between blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block-wise presentation reduces cross-condition contamination and eases sustained adaptation; ensure randomization across subjects to control order effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use method of constant stimuli for target presentation and a 2AFC behavioral task
rubrics_metrics.description: Present test faces drawn from a morph continuum under the method of constant stimuli and require a two-alternative forced choice (2AFC) gender discrimination on each test trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine psychophysical measurement (e.g., Weibull fits) with ERP recording to relate perceptual biases to neural adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a morph continuum of test stimuli (10% steps, omit 50/50 level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate ten test faces ranging from 100% female to 100% male in 10% steps, leaving out the 50/50 midpoint level, using a landmark-based morphing algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using graded morph levels allows analysis of aftereffect magnitude across ambiguity; omit midpoint if needed to avoid undefined responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for low-level visual adaptation (size differences and spatial jitter)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce low-level adaptation confounds, make adapters and targets differ in size and randomize the test stimulus position within a small range (here 1° horizontal/vertical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because N170 is relatively independent of stimulus size, changing size and position helps ensure observed adaptation is not merely low-level retinal adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify and report stimulus sizes and visual angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Report precise stimulus sizes (e.g., NORM: 6.8° × 6.3°, STR: 6.8° × 2.4°), monitor properties (resolution, refresh rate), viewing distance, and background luminance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full reporting of display parameters and visual angles is required for reproducibility and interpreting early ERP components sensitive to retinotopic factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEG recording hardware and electrode montage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Record ERPs with a multi-channel montage (here 32 Ag/AgCl electrodes placed according to the 10/20 system), maintain impedances below ~5 kΩ, sample at high rate (1000 Hz), and report ground and reference sites (ground: FT9, reference: AFz).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full acquisition parameters to enable replication and proper preprocessing choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artifact rejection and retention reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject trials containing blinks, movements, A/D saturation, or baseline drift and report the proportion of trials retained after rejection (here ~92%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state rejection criteria and resulting trial counts per condition to assess signal-to-noise and statistical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering and re-referencing choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply digital filtering (here 0.5–25 Hz zero phase shift) and re-reference averaged data (here to average reference) before analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report filter parameters and referencing scheme because these affect component morphology; use zero-phase filtering to avoid phase distortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define ERP component electrodes and time windows (P100, N170, P200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify electrodes and latency windows for components of interest: P100 measured at O1/O2 (70–130 ms), N170 measured at P7/P8, P9/P10, PO7/PO8, PO9/PO10 (140–210 ms), P200 at O1/O2, P5/P6, PO3/PO4, PO7/PO8 (215–320 ms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use predefined electrode sets and windows for peak detection and ensure consistency across subjects; report how peaks were identified within windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure individual peak amplitude and latency within specified windows
rubrics_metrics.description: For each subject and condition, measure peak amplitude and latency for components within the pre-specified time windows rather than using arbitrary fixed latencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measuring individual peaks captures subject variability; clarify whether peak or mean amplitude is used and how overlapping components are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis: repeated measures ANOVA with corrections and post-hoc tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyse amplitude and latency values with repeated measures ANOVAs including factors such as adapter type, hemisphere, electrode; apply Greenhouse-Geisser correction for non-sphericity and Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report all factors, degrees of freedom (with adjustments), effect sizes (e.g., ηp2), and exact p-values; use appropriate corrections for multiple comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model behavioral psychophysics with Weibull fits (Psignifit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit behavioral choice data using a Weibull psychometric function (Psignifit) to quantify discrimination performance and relate behavioral shifts to adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fit parameters, goodness-of-fit, and use the fits to derive metrics such as point of subjective equality or slope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute aftereffect magnitude as difference between male- and female-adapted endorsement rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate magnitude of the aftereffect by subtracting the percentage of trials endorsed as female during female-adapted conditions from that during male-adapted conditions, separately for configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this computed magnitude in subsequent ANOVAs (e.g., configuration × morph-level) to directly compare adaptation strength across conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collapse across adaptor gender and morph levels when necessary to increase ERP trial counts
rubrics_metrics.description: For ERP categorical adaptation analyses, collapse data across adaptor genders (male/female) and target morph-levels to obtain sufficient trials per ERP average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about collapsing choices and justify them; collapsing increases SNR but sacrifices condition-specific resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of N170 adaptation: reduced amplitude indicates repetition/adaptation and sensitivity to configural properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret reductions in N170 amplitude following repeated face exposure as neural adaptation; smaller adaptation for stretched adapters (STR) than normal adapters (NORM) suggests sensitivity of N170 to second-order relations (CONF2nd) in addition to first-order configural information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider hemisphere- and electrode-specific patterns (e.g., stronger right-hemisphere effects) and compare adapter conditions to CTRL to separate category-level from configuration-specific adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include hemisphere and electrode interactions in analyses and expect lateralization
rubrics_metrics.description: Test for interactions of hemisphere and adapter condition (e.g., adaptation effects may be stronger over the right hemisphere and vary across superior vs inferior electrode sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report electrode × adapter and hemisphere × adapter interactions and examine topographies to localize effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection and ethical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit naive, healthy volunteers with normal or corrected-to-normal vision, obtain written informed consent, and conform to institutional ethical committee protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size, sex composition, mean age ± SD, and ethical approval identifiers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report trial counts, block structure, and total recording time for feasibility and power considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the number of presentations per test stimulus within a block (here each test stimulus presented 5 times yielding 150 trials per block) and total session duration (~90 minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These details help readers assess subject fatigue risk and statistical power; adjust trial counts to balance SNR against participant burden.
